# Signatories and community support

Shaurita D. Hutchins will lead the project in collaboration with Samuel Bharti. Both are PhD candidates at the University of Alabama at Birmingham.

**Hutchins will lead educational design and community development.** She will develop the metadata schema, coordinate example tutorials, and establish accessibility and contribution guidance. A computational biologist trained in genetics, genomics, and bioinformatics, she brings experience in Carpentries instruction and reproducible R/Bioconductor workflows. She received a grant to develop [Prioritizing Candidate Genetic Variants Using GTEx, HuBMAP, and IDG](https://cfdetrainingcenter.github.io/candidate-genetic-variants/) for the Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) Training Center. Built with Quarto Live, the module combines coding activities that run in the browser with knowledge checks.

**Bharti will lead software architecture and engine integration.** He will harden and extend adapters that use existing engine checks and produce validation reports in a common format. A former Posit intern, he brings experience developing Shiny applications and R packages, including bioclients, biohttp, and biobouncer. His teaching work includes [r-for-beginners](https://github.com/samuelbharti/r-for-beginners), an adaptation of Software Carpentry lessons with accompanying slides. He also maintains automated workflows for publishing package documentation through GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.

We will jointly design the package API and registry, and share responsibility for governance and the example tutorials.

We requested public feedback through [r/Stats](https://www.reddit.com/r/Stats/comments/1wvj3wd/for_people_who_teach_or_learn_r_how_do_you_find/) and the [learnr webR discussion](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944771998). Community contributor [\@coatless](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944898742) pointed us to learnr2 and Quarto Live. That feedback helped us focus on shared metadata and checks, though the proposed schema still needs review. We will seek engine maintainers' feedback on the schema and the checks each adapter can support.

We will also consult Carpentries and Bioconductor educators, along with university and community instructors. We will add documented feedback and letters of support as received.
